9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium wide, eye level, Scarlett (Image 2) crosses the rooftop with the lipstick and flower near the ledge, alert to the gusting wind., Handheld lateral composition follows Scarlett (Image 2) toward the low concrete ledge, with the coral flower bobbing in her coat pocket and the skyline opening behind her., EXT. DOWNTOWN ROOFTOP — LATE AFTERNOON. Scarlett (Image 2) climbs onto the rooftop, wind pushing her hair across her face as the city glows warm behind her. She pulls the coral lipstick from her pocket, checks the bullet, and twists it down with a decisive click while a distant train begins to rattle below., downtown_rooftop_warm_skyline_concrete, Late-afternoon golden light washes the skyline and creates warm rim light around Scarlett (Image 2). The exposed rooftop remains naturally bright, with shifting highlights caused by wind and the reflective lipstick surface., Warm amber sunlight, concrete gray, black clothing, hazy blue-gray skyline, steel railing, vivid coral flower, and satin coral lipstick., scarlett_city_influencer, Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
